column1: Design a leaderless replication protocol with sloppy quorums that tolerates network partitions while bounding staleness for read-your-writes consistency.
Implement a token-bucket rate limiter that is consistent across 50 stateless microservice replicas without a single point of failure.
Explain how Raft's leader election handles the split-vote scenario and why randomized timeouts alone are insufficient at high replica counts.
Design a multi-region active-active database architecture that resolves write conflicts using CRDTs for a shopping cart use case.
Implement a distributed lock service using Redis with correct fencing tokens to prevent stale-lock-holder writes.
Design a backpressure-aware message queue architecture connecting 10 producers to a slow consumer without unbounded memory growth.
Explain the trade-offs between chain replication and quorum-based replication for a write-heavy key-value store.
Design a service mesh sidecar retry policy that avoids retry storms during a downstream partial outage.
Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes and explain how you'd rebalance data when a node joins a 200-node cluster.
Design a distributed cron/scheduler service that guarantees exactly-once job execution across a fleet of workers.
Design a Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus protocol with formal safety and liveness proofs for a permissioned blockchain.
Prove that no asynchronous consensus protocol can guarantee both safety and liveness in the presence of even one faulty process (FLP impossibility) and discuss its practical implications for Paxos.
Design a globally distributed transactional database (Spanner-like) with TrueTime-style bounded clock uncertainty and prove external consistency.
Design a novel gossip protocol with provable epidemic convergence bounds under adversarial message loss rates.
Formally verify the safety of a two-phase commit protocol extension that adds a coordinator failover mechanism using TLA+.
Design a self-stabilizing distributed algorithm for leader election that recovers from arbitrary transient faults without external reset.
Prove tight bounds on the message complexity of Byzantine agreement with n=3f+1 replicas under partial synchrony.
Design a CRDT for a collaborative text editor that guarantees convergence under arbitrary operation reordering, with a formal proof of strong eventual consistency.
Implement a lock-free concurrent skip list supporting insertion and deletion, and argue why it avoids the ABA problem without hazard pointers.
Implement a persistent (immutable) red-black tree supporting O(log n) insert with structural sharing, and analyze amortized rebalancing cost.
Design and implement a Fibonacci heap supporting decrease-key in O(1) amortized time and explain its role in Dijkstra's algorithm's O(E + V log V) bound.
Implement a suffix automaton for a string and use it to count distinct substrings in O(n).
Implement a van Emde Boas tree supporting predecessor/successor queries in O(log log U) time for a universe of size U.
Design an algorithm to find the k-th smallest element in the union of two sorted arrays in O(log(m+n)) time, with full correctness proof.
Implement a link-cut tree supporting path queries on a dynamic forest in O(log n) amortized time.
Prove the correctness and analyze the amortized complexity of the union-find data structure with path compression and union by rank.
Design an approximate nearest neighbor search structure (e.g. HNSW) and derive its expected query complexity in high-dimensional space.
Implement a persistent segment tree supporting range updates and historical version queries in O(log n) per operation.
Design an algorithm for the minimum-cost flow problem using successive shortest augmenting paths with Johnson's reweighting, and prove its polynomial runtime.
Prove that determining whether a given planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle remains NP-complete, and discuss known polynomial special cases.
Design a competitive online algorithm for the ski-rental problem and prove its optimal competitive ratio.
Design a streaming algorithm to estimate the number of distinct elements in a data stream using O(log log n) space (HyperLogLog-style) with error analysis.
Derive and prove the time complexity of the Blossom algorithm for maximum matching in general (non-bipartite) graphs.
Design a parallel algorithm for suffix array construction (DC3/skew algorithm) and prove its O(n) work bound.
Prove the existence of an NP-intermediate problem under the assumption P is not NP (Ladner's theorem) and sketch the diagonalization construction.
Design a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for the Euclidean traveling salesman problem and outline Arora's proof of correctness.
Design a sharded, multi-tenant SaaS architecture with per-tenant data isolation, noisy-neighbor mitigation, and online resharding.
Design a real-time bidding (RTB) ad exchange system that must respond within 100ms p99 across geographically distributed exchanges.
Design the architecture for a global content delivery network with dynamic origin shielding and cache invalidation propagation under 1 second.
Design a system for exactly-once event processing in a payment pipeline spanning Kafka, a database, and a third-party payment gateway.
Design a search autocomplete system serving 100k queries/sec with personalized ranking and sub-10ms latency.
Design an architecture for a multiplayer game server handling authoritative state synchronization for 10,000 concurrent players with lag compensation.
Design a feature store architecture supporting both low-latency online serving and batch offline training with point-in-time correctness.
Design a system to detect and mitigate cascading failures in a microservice dependency graph with circuit breakers and adaptive concurrency limits.
Design the full architecture of a stock exchange matching engine capable of handling 1M orders/sec with deterministic ordering and disaster recovery.
Design a planet-scale DNS system with anycast routing, DDoS mitigation, and sub-second failover, and formally justify its availability guarantees.
Derive the backpropagation update rule for a transformer's multi-head self-attention layer including the Jacobian of the softmax, and identify where gradient instability arises.
Explain why increasing model width and depth alone eventually leads to double descent, and derive the bias-variance decomposition that predicts this.
Design a mixture-of-experts routing mechanism with load-balancing auxiliary loss and prove why naive top-1 routing collapses to a subset of experts.
Derive the ELBO for a variational autoencoder and explain the reparameterization trick's role in enabling low-variance gradient estimates.
Explain the mathematical mechanism behind grokking in neural networks and connect it to the loss landscape's implicit regularization.

Derive the convergence rate of the Adam optimizer under non-convex smooth loss assumptions and identify why its second-moment estimate can cause non-convergence (as in the Reddi et al. counterexample).
Design a constitutional-AI-style RLHF pipeline including reward model training, PPO fine-tuning, and KL-penalty tuning, and analyze reward hacking failure modes.
Prove a generalization bound for a neural network using the PAC-Bayes framework and interpret the role of the prior/posterior KL term.
Derive the diffusion model's reverse SDE from the forward noising process and show the equivalence between score matching and denoising objectives.
Design a scaling-law extrapolation experiment to predict the loss of a 1-trillion-parameter model from smaller runs, addressing confounds like data repetition and tokenizer changes.
Prove the universal approximation theorem for a single hidden-layer neural network with sigmoid activations, and discuss why this doesn't explain why depth helps in practice.
Derive the exact expression for the Neural Tangent Kernel of an infinite-width fully-connected network and explain what it implies about training dynamics.
Design a theoretical framework proving sample complexity lower bounds for in-context learning in transformers under a Bayesian meta-learning interpretation.
Prove convergence guarantees for federated averaging (FedAvg) under non-IID client data distributions with partial participation.
Design and prove correctness of a mechanistic-interpretability circuit-finding algorithm for identifying induction heads in a transformer.
Prove the Cayley-Hamilton theorem and use it to derive an O(n^3 log k) algorithm for computing A^k for an n x n matrix.
Prove that the set of algebraic numbers is countable, and explain why this implies almost all real numbers are transcendental.
Prove the spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices and explain its role in PCA's optimality for variance maximization.
Prove that a bipartite graph has a perfect matching if and only if it satisfies Hall's marriage condition.
Derive the Cramer-Rao lower bound for an unbiased estimator and apply it to the variance of the MLE for a Poisson rate parameter.
Prove the Central Limit Theorem via characteristic functions for i.i.d. random variables with finite variance.
Prove Godel's first incompleteness theorem via the construction of a self-referential arithmetic sentence, explaining the role of the diagonal lemma.
Prove the Riemann rearrangement theorem and construct an explicit rearrangement of the alternating harmonic series that converges to an arbitrary target value.
Explain why P vs NP is closely tied to a specific circuit lower bound conjecture, and why current techniques (natural proofs) are believed insufficient to resolve it.
Prove the Banach fixed-point theorem and use it to establish existence and uniqueness of solutions to a first-order ODE (Picard-Lindelof).
Prove the strong duality theorem for linear programming and derive the KKT conditions as its nonlinear generalization.
State and prove the Chinese Remainder Theorem in its ring-theoretic generality, and explain its role in RSA key generation efficiency.
Prove that every finite integral domain is a field, and use it to justify why arithmetic modulo a prime forms a field.
Prove the Cook-Levin theorem: that Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete, by reducing an arbitrary NP language to SAT via a Turing machine tableau construction.
Prove Yao's principle for lower-bounding randomized algorithm complexity and apply it to show a lower bound for comparison-based sorting under adversarial distributions.
Prove the Ax-Grothendieck theorem (an injective polynomial map from C^n to C^n is surjective) using the compactness theorem from model theory.
Explain why a proof of the Yang-Mills mass gap conjecture remains an open Millennium Prize Problem, and outline the mathematical obstacles to a rigorous construction.
Design a padding oracle attack against a CBC-mode encryption scheme and derive the number of queries needed to decrypt a block.
Explain the mathematical structure of the ECDSA nonce-reuse vulnerability and derive the private key recovery equation given two signatures with the same nonce.
Design a formally verified TLS 1.3 handshake state machine and identify which downgrade attacks it must be proven to reject.
Explain how lattice-based cryptography (e.g. Kyber) achieves post-quantum security and derive the hardness assumption it relies on (LWE).
Design a zero-knowledge proof protocol (e.g. zk-SNARK) for proving knowledge of a Sudoku solution without revealing it, including the arithmetic circuit construction.
Prove that textbook RSA encryption is malleable and design a chosen-ciphertext attack exploiting this against a naive signature scheme.
Design a secure multi-party computation protocol for computing the median of private inputs from n parties without revealing individual values.
Explain the mathematics of Shor's algorithm for integer factorization and derive why it breaks RSA in polynomial time on a quantum computer.
Design a side-channel-resistant implementation of AES that defends against cache-timing attacks, and prove why naive table-lookup implementations leak key bits.
Formally define and construct a homomorphic encryption scheme supporting one multiplication and unlimited additions (somewhat homomorphic), and explain noise growth management.
Design a Byzantine-resilient federated learning aggregation rule (e.g. Krum) and prove its resistance to a bounded number of malicious clients.
Design a type inference algorithm (Hindley-Milner) for a small functional language and prove its principal type property.
Implement an optimizing compiler pass performing SSA-based dead code elimination and constant propagation, and prove it preserves program semantics.
Design a garbage collector using generational mark-and-sweep with a write barrier, and analyze its worst-case pause time.
Design a dependent type system supporting Pi and Sigma types and explain how it prevents a specific class of runtime errors that simple types cannot.
Prove type soundness (progress and preservation) for a simply typed lambda calculus with references.
Design a JIT compiler's inline caching mechanism for dynamic method dispatch and analyze its amortized speedup versus polymorphic call sites.
Design a linear type system for a systems programming language that statically prevents use-after-free without a garbage collector.
Explain how continuation-passing style transformation enables implementing first-class exceptions and coroutines, with a formal CPS translation.
Design an algorithm for register allocation via graph coloring, and prove why the problem is NP-hard in general but tractable with chordal interference graphs.
Design a session-typed communication protocol ensuring deadlock-freedom for a set of concurrently communicating processes, with a formal proof sketch.
Design the internal architecture of an LSM-tree storage engine including compaction strategy trade-offs (leveled vs tiered) and write amplification analysis.
Explain how MVCC with snapshot isolation can still permit write skew anomalies, and design a serializable snapshot isolation (SSI) mechanism to prevent it.
Design a B+ tree with copy-on-write pages for crash-consistent storage, and explain how it enables lock-free readers during writer updates.
Design a query optimizer's cost-based join ordering algorithm using dynamic programming, and explain why it becomes intractable beyond roughly 15 tables.
Explain how a write-ahead log combined with checkpointing guarantees ARIES-style crash recovery, detailing the analysis, redo, and undo passes.
Design a distributed SQL query engine that pushes down predicates and aggregations to a sharded storage layer while preserving transactional consistency.
Design a vectorized execution engine for OLAP queries and analyze how SIMD and cache-line alignment affect throughput versus row-at-a-time execution.
Design a formally correct two-phase locking protocol variant that guarantees strict serializability while minimizing lock contention via predicate locking.
Design an index structure (e.g. R-tree or GiST) supporting efficient range queries over multi-dimensional spatial data, with a worst-case query complexity analysis.
Design a database recovery protocol for a system using both a primary-key B-tree and secondary LSM-based indexes that must remain mutually consistent after a crash.
Design a work-stealing scheduler for a user-level thread runtime and prove its expected makespan bound relative to the optimal parallel schedule.
Explain how RCU (read-copy-update) achieves wait-free reads in the Linux kernel, and analyze the trade-off with grace-period-based memory reclamation latency.
Design a memory allocator with per-CPU caching (like tcmalloc) and analyze fragmentation versus contention trade-offs under high concurrency.
Prove that Peterson's algorithm for mutual exclusion between two processes satisfies mutual exclusion and starvation-freedom under sequential consistency.
Design a wait-free concurrent queue implementation and prove why it satisfies linearizability using a formal linearization point argument.
Explain how the Linux CFS scheduler's red-black-tree-based virtual runtime model approximates fair share scheduling, and derive its scheduling latency bound.
Design a formal relaxed memory consistency model and prove that a specific compiler reordering optimization remains safe under it.
Design a NUMA-aware thread and memory placement strategy for a latency-sensitive in-memory database and quantify expected cross-socket access penalties.
Prove the impossibility of implementing a wait-free consensus object using only atomic read/write registers for more than two processes (consensus number argument).
Design a formally verified microkernel IPC mechanism (seL4-style) and explain what properties the functional correctness proof guarantees about isolation.
Derive the Black-Scholes PDE from the assumption of a self-financing replicating portfolio and no-arbitrage, and explain the role of the Feynman-Kac theorem in its solution.
Design a mean-variance portfolio optimization system that incorporates transaction costs and turnover constraints, and derive the resulting quadratic program.
Derive the pricing formula for an American put option under the binomial model and explain why no closed-form solution exists analogous to Black-Scholes.
Design a market-making algorithm that manages inventory risk using an Avellaneda-Stoikov style optimal quoting model, and derive the reservation price formula.
Explain how the Heston stochastic volatility model captures the volatility smile, and derive its characteristic function used for Fourier-based option pricing.
Design a statistical arbitrage strategy using cointegration testing (Johansen test) between a basket of assets, and derive the mean-reversion half-life from an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck fit.
Derive the Kelly criterion for optimal bet sizing under a known edge and variance, and explain why fractional Kelly is used in practice to manage model uncertainty.
Design a value-at-risk and expected shortfall estimation system using historical simulation versus a GARCH-filtered approach, and explain their coverage failure differences under fat tails.
Prove that under the risk-neutral measure, discounted asset prices are martingales, and use this to derive the fundamental theorem of asset pricing's no-arbitrage condition.
Design a limit order book simulation incorporating queue priority and adverse selection, and derive an estimator for the effective bid-ask spread's information component (Glosten-Milgrom style).
